newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia sees GDP rising 13 pct in 1997 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia sees GDP rising 13 pct in 1997 - paper.

text.p: Yugoslavia expects its gross domestic product (GDP) to rise 13 percent next year, Belgrade newspapers reported on Tuesday.
The plan assumed stable prices, a stable dinar currency and a rise in production output and exports, a government report quoted by newspapers said.
It also envisaged further structural changes in the economy and its privatisation, as well as higher living standards of the population, papers said.
But the report added that meeting the targets would be hampered by a shortage of working capital needed to finance greater production and exports.
Normalisation of relations with international financial and commercial bodies, still to be secured, was also noted as a key problem.

The Yugoslav government had expected its 1996 GDP to rise by 12.5 percent. But in October, it said GDP grew only 2.5 percent in the first eight months of the year and said it would fail to reach its goal.
The government revised its earlier forecasts and said GDP this year would likely rise five to six percent to match its 1995 growth rate. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom, 381 11 222 4254
